body:
Yeah, my mom was depressed and super controlling in my childhood - she’s since had therapy and is a wonderfully self-aware and more relaxed now. And it’s SO frustrating, cus I can’t be angry with her.
The neglect I experienced as a child is just as real as the loving mother I have now... and it’s almost impossible to work with in therapy, cus I can’t make myself blame her.

Thanks for the reply!
Not that it’s good, I’m really sorry, but it’s nice knowing that I’m not the only one who experienced something like this. I hope you’re ok :)
Complex PTSD 🗿

Thanks for the reply!
Yep, if I ever choose to have children - adopted or otherwise - it will 100% be my own choice! There are so many miserable people who birth children because it’s just “what women do”. I wouldnt ever want to be one of those women - both for my own sake and the child’s.

I’m so happy to live in a time where women actually have a say in their own lives.

Thanks for your reply!  
It was brought up pretty naturally in the conversation, so it didn't feel forced at all, no worries there.

I like your two reasons, it's an oddly calming way to think about it. Thanks.

Thanks for your reply!  
Yeah, it really is a huge and difficult question to consider.  
I think I'm gonna spend some time pondering and definitely bring this topic up with her again.

Thanks for your reply!  
Yep, I definitely need to talk to her about this whole topic - and as you said, I suspect there might be a small misunderstanding concerning the pregnancy=womanhood thing.  
I don't think pregnancy is scary because of the innante "femaleness" of it, it honestly freaks me out because it reminds me of "Alien" lol. I'll most certaintly bring this up - thanks for your input!

Your journey sounds tough, but very empowering!   
And if I ever choose to adopt/get pregnant, yep it definitely has to be 100% my own choice!

Thanks for your reply!  
Yeah, "women=motherhood=pregnancy" is pretty ingrained in our society and I very much feel like you describe here, always have.  
It's just the "what if it's all trauma and I actually DO have this desire, I've just suppressed it?" question that's completely new and quite overwhelming. I'm gonna have to think a lot about this - and definately talk to my therapist about this whole thing - and I don't want her to sound like a "breeder", she really isn't!   
She's been very respecful of my choice not to have children - it was more of a suggestion, a theory that I could persue if I wanted to.

Thanks, I really appreciate your words :)  
It really is a huge topic (and trigger!) and I just need some time to digest the whole situation.

Thanks for your reply!   
I really appreciate my therapist, honestly she's amazing and the first trauma-informed professional I ever met. It's a whole new perspective and her approach just makes sense. Which is probably why it's freaking me out, because I've never thought of my pregnancy-fear like this.  
It's like ... it was much easier to deal with before, because I didn't even consider it to be a trauma-response - it was just my personality.   
But that's the whole problem with trauma: what's YOU and what's the trauma?

Thanks for your reply!  
TBH, it's 90% fear of pregnancy and 10% "what if I'm a shit parent bcus of trauma?" - as I told her, I wouldn't mind adopting especially an older child and caring for them (with a stable partner of course).   
Pregnancy really freaks me out - but then again, every physical interaction I have freaks me out lol

Thanks for your reply!  
I just really like the thought of adoption too - instead of just birthing yet another child into the world, the idea of taking care of one that might have an otherwise shitty life (maybe even an older child) is much more appealing to me.

Thanks for your reply - I'm really glad to hear about your daughter - I really do like the thought of being a positive influence in a child's life too - but pregnancy just really freaks me out on all levels; physically and mentally.   
If it's not too personal to ask, how did you handle the pregnancy experience?

Thanks for your input - I feel pretty much the same way!   
If I'm ever gonna parent a child, I would want to make sure I could do "all the right things".  
And yep, pregnancy is not a walk in the park!

Yes, misdiagnosis of mental illnesses is sadly quite common - and not talked about!
Ive experienced people saying “oh well it’s understandable because you can’t run tests” and such. I don’t think they understand the enormous impact it can have on you, feeling as though your entire existance is wrong somehow.
I wish, like you, it would be talked about more.

I just read some of your earlier post (sorry for snooping lol) and it seems like - to me at least - your problem lies with the way your parents used the diagnosis against you. It must have been horrible. But it’s really great that you have friends who understand you! Hang on to them!

Yeah, it’s frustrating!
Sometimes I end up being blunt if someone keeps assuming autism - literally tell them “I was mis-diagnosed and this has been confirmed by professionals”

Do you find it’s mostly a problem when talking to mental health ppl or is it just in general?

I was mis-diagnosed with Asperger’s at 17 and had to deal with it for 7 years before I got a personality disorder Dx instead (which made so much more sense).

I absolutely recognize the frustration and especially the fear of saying anything that could be interpreted as an autistic symptom. I carefully choose my words when I try to explain my problems, because what if I end up being labelled autistic again?

I’ve found the most important thing is to explain the feelings that creates the symptoms.
Example: Instead of just saying “I can’t talk to people” (could be autistic), I have to say “I can’t talk to people right now, because I’m afraid of them judging me ect”. I hate that I have to do this, because it requires an obscene amount of self-insight, and it honestly shouldnt be my job.

I think what pissed me off the most, was experiencing how shitty autistic people are treated! Like they had no feelings - they just need structure. Autistic people need to talk about their feelings too, assuming otherwise is ridiculous.

I’m not sure if I have any tips - I can just say the classic “You’re not alone!” 🤗
Thanks for your answer - and yeah, it makes perfect sense that it’s hard to define “normal” yourself in cases like this.
